scenario.title: A settlement batch, and the four ways a scheme misbehaves
scenario.summary: Three payments are released to a simulated scheme. One settles, one is returned, one is never answered; along the way the scheme repeats itself and then contradicts itself. The ledger sand table follows the money.

releaseAudit.label: PARTIAL
releaseAudit.statement: RELEASE AUDIT: PARTIAL. Charter items 1-4 of 8 were performed (migrations replayed from empty; full suite; cross-document consistency; the partial-set sweep). Items 5-7 were NOT performed - standing-lessons compliance, known-debt reconciliation, and the synthetic-data/neutrality sweep - because the external auditor's compute quota was exhausted mid-audit. Closed under the recorded resource-interruption fallback; the uncovered items carry forward as mandatory-first scope for ref-2.

scopeStatement.disclaimer: CloFin operates on synthetic data only. It is not connected to any bank, payment scheme or central bank, holds no regulatory authorisation, and never processes real funds.

amounts.note: Money crosses the API as an integer count of minor units. Every `display` string in this bundle was produced from the adjacent minorUnits by the system's own formatter, in clofin-core, at capture time — never in a browser.

steps.title: What you are about to watch
steps.narrative: A batch of three payments is released to a simulated scheme. One settles, one comes back, and one is never answered. Along the way the scheme answers the same thing twice and then contradicts itself. The three account balances are captured after each event.

steps.title: An organisation to act in
steps.narrative: A second organisation, for the settlement scenario.

steps.title: Seed a maker, a checker and a controller
steps.narrative: No role holds both `payment/approve` and `settlement/execute`: the actor who agreed a payment is never the actor who pushes it out of the door.

steps.narrative: The simulated scheme reads the last digit of the creditor account: 0–6 settles.

steps.narrative: A different actor, holding `approver`, agrees it.

steps.narrative: 7 and 8 come back.

steps.title: A fourth payment, left in draft
steps.narrative: Raised so that it can be refused a place in the batch.

steps.title: An unapproved payment cannot be batched
steps.narrative: One refusal lists every ineligible instruction with its reason, so an operator batching forty payments fixes them in one pass. Nothing is created.

steps.narrative: `replayed` is true and the outcome is the original one, reproduced rather than re-derived. The response count does not move.

steps.title: A late contradiction
steps.narrative: A new message — its replay key is free — claiming the settled payment came back. Refused.
